title: Default bits_per_symbol inference narrows the sample width from the data and changes n×H_bitstring by up to 2.4×; the inferred width is not recorded in the JSON
body:
## Summary

When `bits_per_symbol` is omitted (the documented default), `read_file_subset` (`cpp/shared/utils.h`, "Do we need to establish the word size?") sets `word_size` to the position of the highest bit set in the OR of all bytes. Constant-zero high bits are therefore dropped from the bitstring, and both the bitstring and the `n` in `n × H_bitstring` (§3.1.3) change. This is an undocumented symbol-space reduction: §3.2.2 requirement 6 has the submitter document the fixed symbol size, and §6.4 permits reducing n-bit samples to m bits only via a submitter-supplied bit ranking.

## Reproduction

Built at `87c104d` (macOS, Apple clang + libomp; `selftest` agrees with `refdata` to 3.7e-10).

```
python3 -c "import random;r=random.Random(2);open('w4.bin','wb').write(bytes(r.randrange(16) for _ in range(1000000)))"
./ea_non_iid -vv w4.bin
#   Loaded 1000000 samples of 16 distinct 4-bit-wide symbols
#   H_bitstring Per Symbol = 3.7390649510685936   H_original = 3.7798741076670073
#   Assessed min entropy: 3.7390649510685936
./ea_non_iid -vv w4.bin 8
#   Warning: Symbols appear to be narrower than described.
#   H_bitstring Per Symbol = 1.5385994915639978   H_original = 3.7798741076670073
#   Assessed min entropy: 1.5385994915639978
python3 -c "d=bytearray(open('w4.bin','rb').read());d[-1]|=0x80;open('w4b.bin','wb').write(d)"
./ea_non_iid -vv w4b.bin
#   Loaded 1000000 samples of 17 distinct 8-bit-wide symbols
#   Assessed min entropy: 1.5386114654846945   (one sample changed the width, and the figure, by 2.4x)
```

H_original is invariant (the translation is order-preserving); the n × H_bitstring term is computed on a different bitstring with a different n. The inferred-width figure is 2.4× the declared-width figure here, and a single sample with a high bit set flips it discontinuously. `bin/truerand_4bit.bin` takes the same path.

The "Symbols appear to be narrower than described" warning is printed to stdout; `errorLevel` stays 0 and the message does not reach the JSON report, so a consumer of `-o` output cannot tell which width was used.

## Request

Either require `bits_per_symbol` (or a `--infer-width` opt-in), or record the inferred width and the "narrower than described" condition in the JSON report with a non-zero `errorLevel`/warning field. Which width is normative is a spec-reading question; the point of this issue is that the tool currently decides it silently.

Found while auditing this tool for a downstream use that prices output length on the reported min-entropy figure.
